key_insight: In 2D glasses under cyclic shear, the time to fatigue failure diverges as a power law near the fatigue limit with an exponent close to -1, indicating dimensionality changes how failure accelerates.
engineering_relevance: This suggests fatigue-life prediction in disordered solids may need dimension-aware models, while plastic-activity metrics still provide robust indicators of damage buildup before failure.
method: Atomistic simulations of 2D model glasses under cyclic shear deformation.
Measured failure cycles as strain amplitude approached the fatigue limit.
Used isoconfigurational seeded simulations with a localized soft region to probe variability and failure localization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a power-law divergence of failure cycles near the fatigue limit, scaling of dissipated work and non-affine displacements with failure time, and a broad distribution of failure times even with seeding.
watch_item: Results are from 2D model glasses and may not transfer directly to real materials or to 3D systems without recalibration of the failure exponent and stochasticity.
paper_title: Fatigue failure in two-dimensional glasses under cyclic shear deformation
